subject: Clarify streaming SLA: initial-byte vs sustained tokens/sec commitments
messages:
From: Nina Patel <nina@cloudwave.com>
To: hiro_tanaka@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify streaming SLA: TTFT vs sustained tokens/sec commitments

Hi Hiro / Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — we like Redwood's latency profile overall. Before we move the pilot to production, our SRE team has asked us to get firm language around streaming behavior. Specifically: 1) a time-to-first-token (TTFT) commitment for streaming endpoints (we'd like to target <=300ms for prompts up to 64 tokens), and 2) a guaranteed sustained tokens/second rate for long-running streams (our typical workloads sustain ~45 tps but we need burst to 200 tps for short bursts).

I've attached our suggested redlines to the Master Services Agreement (CloudWave_SLA_Redlines.pdf). We're not asking to change your product — just to include an exception or carveout in the SLA that guarantees a minimum initial-byte performance and a baseline sustained throughput for our dedicated pool, with a fallback behavior we can rely on if those limits aren't met.

Can you confirm whether those two items are workable and, if so, what the mechanics would be (dedicated routing, priority queuing, metrics, and runbooks)? We'd like to lock language before our procurement kickoff next week.

Thanks,
Nina
Head of Platform
CloudWave Systems
[attachment: CloudWave_SLA_Redlines.pdf (pdf)]

From: hiro_tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.com>

Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 12:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify streaming SLA: TTFT vs sustained tokens/sec commitments

Hi Nina — thanks for sending the redlines and for outlining the SRE asks. Short answers up front: yes, we can propose a carveout, and yes, it will likely involve a dedicated routing policy and some observability additions.

High level proposal (we'll formalize):
- TTFT: target <=300ms for streaming endpoints for initial chunk <=64 tokens when routed to a dedicated pool. 
- Sustained throughput: baseline guarantee of 60 tokens/sec per concurrent stream with short burst allowance to 250 tokens/sec for up to 30s, dependent on quota and pool capacity.
- Fallback: automatic fallback to hybrid synchronous endpoint where we commit sustained throughput but may have higher TTFT; customer gets routed and notified.
- Metrics & runbook: we will provide token-level metrics (TTFT, tokens/sec, percentile) and a joint runbook for incident handling.

We'll need legal to review explicit language and we need to map to an appropriate Dedicated capacity commitment (reserved GPUs). Karthik — can you sketch the infra/ops changes (routing and queueing) and confirm impact on other Dedicated customers? Lauren — can you prep the procurement play (pricing delta for reserved pool + monitoring)?

I can join a short call today if helpful.

—Hiro
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding CloudWave's redlines and Nina's note. Key asks: TTFT <=300ms for initial chunk (<=64 tokens) and sustained baseline ~45 tps with bursts to 200+ for short periods. They want this codified in an SLA amendment prior to procurement.

Notes and risks:
- TTFT guarantees require us to lock routing to a dedicated pool for their tenant or a strong isolation policy; otherwise noisy neighbors can blow the initial arrival. That has cost implications (reserved GPUs).
- Sustained tokens/sec guarantee is effectively an admission control promise. If we under-provision we either throttle or violate SLA. We should couple the guarantee to committed capacity + a measured traffic profile (p50/p95 traffic shape) and include an explicit outage/fallback clause.
- Suggested mitigation: offer an amendment that applies only when traffic meets an agreed throughput profile and is routed to a dedicated, pre-warmed pool. Include a clear remediation and credits table (e.g., credit for repeated TTFT misses >3/day).

Proposed draft hook for legal to work from (high-level):
"For streaming endpoints, Redwood will provide an Initial Byte Commitment and a Sustained Throughput Commitment when (a) Customer purchases Dedicated streaming capacity as specified in Schedule X, and (b) Customer provides expected traffic profile and acceptable burst characteristics. Redwood's Initial Byte Commitment is defined as the 95th-percentile time-to-first-token for initial response <= 300ms for payloads <=64 tokens when routed to Dedicated streaming capacity. Sustained Throughput Commitment is defined as a guaranteed baseline of 60 tokens/sec per concurrent stream with a burst allowance to 250 tokens/sec for periods not exceeding thirty (30) seconds, subject to the limits specified in Schedule X. Failure by Redwood to meet these commitments shall trigger remediation procedures and credits as described in Section Y."

Marissa — can you turn the above into contract language and propose credit thresholds? Karthik — what are the ops assumptions (pre-warm, queueing, fallback)?

—Hiro

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: hiro_tanaka@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed amendment language: Streaming initial-byte and sustained throughput commitments 

Hi Nina — thanks for the clear ask and for walking the redlines through with Hiro. Attached is a clean markup and an amendment we can sign that captures the carveout for Dedicated streaming endpoints. Key points included in the amendment:

- Scope: applies only when Customer purchases Dedicated streaming capacity (Schedule X).
- Definitions: explicit definitions for Initial Byte Commitment (TTFT) and Sustained Throughput Commitment (tokens/sec), with measurement methodology (95th percentile over a 30-day rolling window).
- Commitments: TTFT <=300ms for first token (<=64 token initial chunk) when routed to Dedicated pool; Sustained baseline 60 tokens/sec with burst up to 250 tokens/sec for bursts not exceeding 30 seconds and only within the committed pool quota.
- Fallback & remediation: automatic traffic routing to the hybrid synchronous endpoint and a credit schedule if repeated misses occur (3+ misses in a day => credit tier 1).
- Observability: Redwood will publish per-tenant metrics (TTFT, tokens/sec p50/p95/p99) and provide a joint runbook and escalation path.

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached amendment (attachment: CloudWave_SLA_Redlines.pdf) and confirm the measurement windows you require.
2) If the language looks good, we've prepared an amendment signature packet via DocuSign: https://docusign.com/tx/CW-AMEND-4821.
3) Upon signature, we'll schedule an onboarding runbook session and pre-warm the Dedicated pool.

We're happy to tweak the measurement windows or credit thresholds—let us know the team's preference.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Redwood Inference
